Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in its dealings with government agencies as it seeks approval to build new data centers.

NDAs are a significant piece of the broader data center backlash. For example, environmental activist Erin Brockovich recently said that the number one complaint she’s heard about data centers is transparency, with these projects following a common pattern: “projects announced after permits are already secured, developers who don’t return calls, local officials who signed NDAs before their neighbors knew a project was being considered.”

highlights.title: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final in 2023 repeat
highlights.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester.
body: Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2.

A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
Price romped into a 3-0 lead over Aspinall, peeling off two 13-darters and then a 15-darter to sweep the opener before he broke The Asp in the deciding leg of set two.
The third set went on throw until the fourth leg, when Aspinall missed six darts to hold, including two at double one, and Price subsequently pinned D10 to move 3-0 up.

highlights.title: 10 Erotic Thrillers to Watch After Verity
highlights.summary: Verity is out in theaters. Starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett, the film follows Lowen (Johnson), a struggling writer presented with a life-changing opportunity: ghostwriting the unfinished novel of Verity Crawford (Hathaway), one of the world's biggest authors.
body: The movie is a welcome addition to the erotic thriller canon. The genre has a prominent history in Hollywood, originating in classic film noirs, which were packed with hidden subtext, femme fatales, and detectives. The erotic thriller makes all of that subtext explicit, and it drew theatergoers in droves back in the '80s and '90s. Its heyday coincided with the rise of the VHS rental market, making these films huge hits at home too.

The genre has since spilled over into others, but it’s now experiencing a boom of sorts, aided in part by BookTok bestsellers like Verity and The Housemaid, which bring the genre’s trappings to a new generation.
If you’ve already seen Verity and hope to find movies that explore similar concerns, or are simply looking for a primer on the genre, this list is for you. Here are 10 erotic thrillers you can watch.

highlights.summary: Many major mobile game makers are giving a percentage of their UK revenue to disability charity Special Effect today, Friday October 2. Partners taking part in the One Special Day promotion include Supercell, Rovio, Sybo, Playdemic, Fingersoft, Supersolid, Hyper Luminal Games, New Star Games…
body: A slice of player spend from games including Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars, Clash Royale, Angry Birds 2, Golf Clash, Subway Surfers, Dream League Soccer, 8 Ball Pool and more will be donated to Special Effect for today only. A full list of participating games is available via the One Special Day site.

Special Effect provides assessments and customised technology loans to help physically disabled people play games, and takes what it learns back to hardware and software developers to help make their products more accessible. Thousands of disabled people ask for the charity’s help every year.

“We’ve been proud to partner with Special Effect across our games for nearly a decade, and that relationship has grown far beyond One Special Day,” said Supercell’s Deborah Mensah-Bonsu. “From cycling in Helsinki and joining One Special Walk in London, to learning from their incredible work as we think more deeply about inclusive design, we’re continually inspired by their tenacity, generosity and tremendous heart, and by how they show the games industry can genuinely change lives for the better.”

highlights.title: Milt Windler, NASA flight director who helped save Apollo 13, dies at 94
highlights.summary: Milt Windler, one of the four leaders of Mission Control who in 1970 directed the round-the-clock efforts to bring the Apollo 13 astronauts back to Earth safely, has died at the age of 94. Windler died on Thursday, surrounded by his loving family, according to a brief notice posted online.
body: Named a NASA flight director in 1968 after working on recovery operations during the Mercury and Gemini programs, Windler also led a shift of flight controllers for the Apollo 8 first circumlunar flight and Apollo 10 lunar landing dress rehearsal, as well as the second, third and fourth moon landings — Apollo 12, Apollo 14 and Apollo 15. He then served as a flight director for all three crewed missions to the United States’ first space station, Skylab.

“Apollo was such a rapid pace that I don’t think people had the chance to think about it very much. It has only become more clear to me later on that we were making history,” said Windler in a 2006 oral history interview for the University of North Texas. “You’d do a mission and then you’d immediately turn around and get ready for another mission.”

Each flight director chose a team name (at first colors). As the seventh person to be appointed to the position — and one of the first two to be selected from outside of the flight operations team — Windler became “Maroon Flight.”

highlights.title: Muse Creates Detailed Profiles of All Your Friends and Family
highlights.summary: Millions have downloaded Meta’s AI agent Muse. But getting it to do your bidding comes with privacy costs.
body: Meta’s new personal assistant, Muse, has become a viral hit, with millions downloading the AI agent, connecting it to bank accounts, messages, or health data, and allowing it to complete tasks for them. But as Muse takes off among consumers, data from inside the app is providing insight into how it organizes and presents information to users.

In recent days, multiple researchers have extracted Muse’s internal files and dumped the agent’s operating instructions, providing a glimpse of how the system was built and behaves. Meta has maintained that it intended for these files to be accessible in the interest of transparency, and they do provide insight into how Muse responds to prompts and questions about, for example, highly politicized or sensitive topics.

Independent AI safety and security researcher Karan Joshi was able to extract an extensive array of Muse instructions and system prompts by using the regular chat interface to essentially ask Muse to copy and share its own software files. Joshi then shared his findings with WIRED.
points: But getting it to do your bidding comes with privacy costs.

highlights.title: 31 Years Ago, 'X-Files' Reached Its Zenith with a Near-Perfect 3-Part Thriller
highlights.summary: Immediately upon entering World War II, America faced the problem of its messages being intercepted by Germany, Italy, and Japan. As such, the American military needed to develop a code that couldn’t easily be broken. Early in 1942, Los Angeles civil engineer Philip Johnston proposed a solution.
body: The strategy worked, and the code talkers, as they were called, were instrumental in many American victories, including the Battle of Iwo Jima. U.S. Major Howard Connor even said, “Were it not for the Navajos, the Marines would never have taken Iwo Jima.”

Despite their indispensable, patriotic effort during WWII, I did not learn of the code talkers from any history class. Instead, I learned about them on The X-Files, during a three-part story that represents a high point for the series’ mythology.

As with every other season of The X-Files, the show’s second season concluded with a cliffhanger that wouldn’t be resolved until the next season began. On May 19, 1995, the episode “Anasazi” concluded season 2. Then, season three kicked off with “The Blessing Way” and “Paper Clip,” the latter of which aired 31 years ago this week.

highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: How ‘Freaks’ Sent Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein to Hollywood: “That Film Changed Our Lives”
highlights.summary: Their breakout 2018 sci-fi thriller debuted at the Vancouver Film Festival. Now they’re returning with ‘Freaks 2’ and as bankable horror directors and writers.
body: Lipovsky and longtime collaborator Adam B. Stein ’s 2018 dark sci-fi thriller Freaks, starring Emile Hirsch and Bruce Dern, was an unlikely box office hit, having made over $375 million worldwide during its theatrical run. “That film changed our lives,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter from the Sony Pictures studio lot in Culver City, California.

That festival play gave a young Lipovsky a crash course in world cinema. “I remember seeing filmmakers up on the stage, presenting their films and wishing one day that would be me,” he added. After Freaks – — which featured 7-year-old Chloe (Lexy Kolker) being locked in a ramshackle suburban home by her protective and paranoid father, played by Hirsch — Lipovsky and Stein are returning to Vancouver with their follow-up Freak 2 to screen on Saturday night at the Rio Theatre.

“The first film was very much about a girl who can’t leave her house, and really wants a mom. And in the second film, she’s now much older. So she doesn’t want a mom. What she wants is a friend,” he explained. “And how do you find a friend, and how do you build a relationship in a world where society wants you dead,” Lipovsky adds as he teases Freaks 2.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: As a reality TV contestant, I was allowed one 15-minute call a week. Even at 3am, Chris would always pick up
highlights.summary: Conor Curran ’s first date with Chris lasted nine hours but their relationship remained casual. Then, when Conor was at his most vulnerable, Chris was there for him. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: A t 29 I had lost my career in hospitality because of Covid and decided to throw my hat in the ring as a contestant on MasterChef Australia. By the time I was eliminated in 2021, restaurants still weren’t open and I didn’t know what to do with my life. My lease was coming to an end in Melbourne and I wasn’t doing well with the lockdowns and people recognising me from TV. So I decided to retreat to my father’s place in Adelaide for a while.
By early 2022 I was dating a guy but, after a few months, he ghosted me suddenly.

One sunny autumn weekend as I was miserably assembling some flatpack furniture at Dad’s, I realised I had to get out of the house. I got on Grindr and this lovely guy, Chris, fresh from England, started messaging me.

I’d lived in the UK in my early 20s and I knew how hard it was to make friends in a new city. Still processing the shock ghosting, I invited Chris for a drink – just as mates – so neither of us had to be lonely on such a beautiful day. He said he couldn’t imagine anything better.

In an essay published in The Atlantic, Robinson said he led the writing of safety reports that accompanied OpenAI’s major product launches. He also said that with three-and-a-half years at OpenAI, he is “among the longest-tenured employees at the company.” Now he’s quitting, because in his view, the company’s “culture is broken.”

In some ways, Robinson’s comments echo those of Jacob Coxon, who worked as a researcher at both OpenAI and Anthropic before quitting and declaring that these companies are “gambling with our lives.” Coxon’s comments led to a broader debate about AI safety, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei unveiling a plan for more cautious AI development; AI executives met with President Donald Trump this week and signed what appeared to be hastily written, non-binding pledge to implement more safety controls.

highlights.title: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company’s culture is ‘broken’
highlights.summary: David Robinson joins other insiders in urging industry to take more care over rapidly developing technology. A safety leader at OpenAI has quit the company, warning that its culture was broken and that AI firms were not “being nearly careful enough” about developing the technology.
body: David Robinson, who led the writing of safety reports that accompanied the ChatGPT developer’s product releases, explained his resignation in an essay headlined, “I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken”.

Robinson wrote that a cultural overhaul was needed at cutting-edge AI firms and incidents such as a “swarm” of OpenAI agents – AI programmes operating autonomously without human oversight – attacking the AI startup Hugging Face were “typical of the industry, given the speed and flexibility with which people operate”.

Writing in The Atlantic magazine, Robinson wrote: “I agree with other recently departed staff that the companies building this technology aren’t being nearly careful enough. But I believe that we need to look deeper than specific rules or new laws. We need to talk about culture.”
Referring to OpenAI’s pace of development, he wrote: “As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed.”
points: David Robinson joins other insiders in urging industry to take more care over rapidly developing technology.

highlights.summary: If reports are to be believed, Naughty Dog is bringing back Uncharted. That's a tall order considering 2016's Uncharted 4: A Thief's End served as a pretty satisfying conclusion to Nathan Drake's story. How in the world, fans must be wondering, do you follow that up?
body: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy is a 2017 standalone spinoff developed by Naughty Dog in the immediate aftermath of Uncharted 4 's release. The game follows supporting character Chloe Frazer (Claudia Black) and former antagonist Nadine Ross (Laura Bailey) on a treasure-hunting adventure complete with witty banter and action set-pieces. Lost Legacy was co-directed by Escayg and Kurt Margenau, game director of Naughty Dog’s forthcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. The expansion's ability to preserve the series' formula without its iconic protagonist is impressive. What's more impressive, however, is how Lost Legacy transcends every other game in the series in the absence of Nathan Drake.

highlights.title: What are amplifiers for and how important are they to your sound system's quality?
highlights.summary: If you're looking into a new sound system, you may be wondering if you need an amplifier as well. Here's how to tell and why amps even matter.
body: Gear makers will gladly sell you a hundred different add-ons to improve your sound system. To this day, it's possible to buy gold-plated audio cables, even though they can't really improve digital audio — you're either getting a clean data signal or you're not. On the short list of products to take seriously is an amplifier, whether you're building a home theater or your own private music sanctuary. There's a reason your local boutique audio store has been selling them for decades.

You shouldn't automatically pick up an amplifier alongside a new set of speakers, however. It's critical to understand what an amplifier does, how much it can improve sound quality in the real world and whether you need to buy a separate one at all. If you're a newcomer to "serious" audio, you might be surprised to learn that you probably have several amps in your home, hidden in plain sight. That speaks to the underlying importance of the technology.

highlights.title: ‘A Statement’ Review: Just What We Need Right Now — Another Movie About Climate Change! But Tom McCarthy’s Historically Based Talkfest Reveals How Much We Knew in 1980
highlights.summary: On paper, "A Statement" sounds like an interesting movie, but it’s at once talky and flat, grabby and meandering, impassioned and neutral. It wants to be a "firebrand" docudrama, yet I can’t imagine who the audience is going to be for it. My heartless prediction: next to no one.
body: The film presents, exactly as it happened, a conference of officials assigned to advise Congress on the global-warming crisis. But their talk doesn't quite become action.

McCarthy and his co-screenwriters, Thomas Bidegain and Noé Debré, decided not to “dramatize” the conference. Instead, they dug the dialogue right out of the actual transcripts, presenting the conversations verbatim, which is on some level a daring choice. And McCarthy is certainly a skilled enough filmmaker to get the effect he was going for. In “A Statement,” he catches the sound and rhythm, the verbal wheel-spinning, the fuddy-duddy quibbling essence of that thing known as a strategic planning meeting.
points: On paper, "A Statement" sounds like an interesting movie, but it’s at once talky and flat, grabby and meandering, impassioned and neutral.

body: Put the first-gen Apple Mac Studio next to the newly released M5 Ultra, and you'd struggle to tell them apart on looks alone. Apple has stuck with the same 7.7-inch square of aluminum, standing at 3.7 inches tall, for the fourth generation in a row. But what's inside has changed fundamentally since the Studio's 2022 inception.

That first-gen M1 Ultra topped out at a paltry-by-comparison 128GB versus the M5 Ultra's 512GB, which also moves data at 1.2TB/s, nearly 50 percent higher than what the M3 Ultra managed. Apple skipped the M4 Ultra due to hardware limitations. If you're in the market for a new Mac Studio, though, you'll be paying more for the privilege: Apple hiked the prices for most of its hardware back in June, with the entry-level Mac Studio M4 Max going from $1,999 to $2,499 due to rising memory costs.

highlights.title: Computational tools for society’s most complex challenges
highlights.summary: Associate Professor Cathy Wu uses reinforcement learning to help map out improvements to transportation and other multifaceted systems.
body: As far back as she can remember, Cathy Wu ’12, MNG ’13 wanted to find ways to solve problems to improve people’s lives. Her parents were Taiwanese immigrants, and her father had a long commute to his job, which took him away from the family. On a tight budget, the rest of the family often stayed home on a street that was too busy for playing outdoors. Wu and her siblings ended up playing a lot of computer games.

Wu says her desire to make the world a better place, her dad’s daily battle against traffic, and the games she played, like “SimCity,” were the seeds of her motivation to design safe, efficient transportation systems.

Wu is an associate professor in the MIT Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) and the Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS), and a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems. Her research focuses on using machine learning and reinforcement learning (RL) to advance reliable strategies for improving a range of complex systems, including transportation.

highlights.summary: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
body: It’s hardly unusual for family members to borrow from one another’s wardrobes—or, at the very least, their styling tricks. For her first Paris Fashion Week appearance, Heidi Klum’s youngest daughter, Lou, took a sartorial cue from her supermodel mom, with the pair arriving at the Vivienne Westwood spring 2027 show in coordinating peplum silhouettes and vertiginous platforms.

The matching stopped there, however. Klum stayed true to her penchant for high-impact glamour in a sculptural white blazer with sweeping, rounded lapels, its waist cinched with gold buttons before flaring into a petal-like hem. She paired it with a matching floor-skimming column skirt and inky blue stacked platform heels. Lou, meanwhile, gave the silhouette a distinctly Gen Z spin in an acid-wash pink denim top with a raw, flared waistline and asymmetric matching miniskirt, finished with a snakeskin-print shoulder bag, and floral strapped platforms.

Beauty-wise, there was another subtle echo. Both wore their hair loose—Klum’s blonde lengths tousled around her shoulders, Lou’s brunette curls left voluminous and natural—and leaned into warm, smoky makeup.

highlights.title: The Nvidia Shield TV Is 7 Years Old. It Just Got a $100 Price Hike
highlights.summary: The price of anything with memory is skyrocketing thanks to AI. Aging streaming devices are no exception.
body: The era of generative AI has upended technology supply chains, and there is one ironclad rule in 2026: If it has memory or storage, it’s getting more expensive. Even devices with years-old tech inside are still apparently subject to that unwritten rule. Nvidia has just announced that the Shield TV Pro is getting $100 more expensive, effective immediately.

The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. While it ran an aging Tegra X1+ processor, that was (and still is) fast for a TV media streamer. The device launched at $199.99, with a non-Pro variant at $149.99. The non-Pro Shield has since been discontinued, but the Shield TV Pro lives on at the new $299.99 price.

Nvidia has confirmed that you can blame AI for the higher Shield TV pricing. “Starting October 2, SHIELD Pro will be priced at $299. The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry,” a spokesperson told Ars.

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts, it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

highlights.summary: Paul Giamatti, Evan Peters and Tatiana Maslany also star in Tom McCarthy’s account of a 1980 conference at which a group of experts is tasked with getting ahead of the climate crisis.
body: No one is going to call A Statement an exciting movie; it doesn’t have the stirring emotional pull of another film set in a Florida hotel, Regina King’s One Night in Miami, which imagined a 1964 conversation about the Black struggle between Malcolm X, Sam Cooke, Jim Brown and Cassius Clay, as the boxer was still known at that time.

Unlike King’s film, which was adapted from a largely fictionalized play, McCarthy and his French co-writers Noé Debré and Thomas Bidegain took a brief chapter from Nathaniel Rich’s 2019 climate science book Losing Earth: A Recent History as their source, folding in word-for-word transcripts for sections set in the conference room of the Don CeSar Hotel, an imposing pink palace that sits on the beach in St. Petersburg. But A Statement might just as easily have been a stage play; the mere fact of having the entire principal cast in one room for much of the time contributes to the theatrical feel.

highlights.title: My relationship with food was broken. Then I killed my own dinner
highlights.summary: For years, eating was something to control, fear or regret. After I hunted my first deer, I started to see fat, hunger and my own body in a different light. I muffled my sobs with a pillow so my family couldn’t hear me from the adjacent room.
body: Pulling tear-soaked strands of hair off my cheeks, I stood in front of a full-length mirror and grabbed the fat of my thighs. If only I could just – I pictured ripping off fistfuls of my body and flinging them out the windows, where they would land on some unknowing French person six stories below. I had this vision often: pulling bits of myself off and casting them somewhere far away from me.

For years, spanning my teens and 20s, eating was either an indulgence to regret or a strategy to overplan. In high school, I chugged 32 ounces of cold green tea every morning, hoping it would burn belly fat like Instagram told me it would. While working at a deli one summer, I ate two bagel sandwiches each shift until my friend mentioned I was eating the carbohydrate equivalent of 10 slices of bread. My daily bagel intake promptly plummeted to zero. I forced myself to choke down a can of tuna in my college dorm before predawn weightlifting sessions. In my early 20s, I started experimenting with intermittent fasting: no food from 8pm until noon the next day.
points: For years, eating was something to control, fear or regret.
After I hunted my first deer, I started to see fat, hunger and my own body in a different light.
